newsitem.title: ZAIRE: U.N. planes evacuate aid workers from Zaire.
newsitem.headline: U.N. planes evacuate aid workers from Zaire.

text.p: Two U.N. planes evacuated a total of 128 U.N. and other expatriate aid workers and some other foreigners from the eastern Zairean town of Bukavu on Saturday and headed for Uganda.
U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) spokeswoman Brenda Barton said the planes left Bukavu safely at 5.35 p.m. for Entebbe airport in Uganda and then Nairobi, Kenya.

She said those aboard were believed to be the last foreign aid workers in Bukavu after the U.N. ordered the evacuation because of rising insecurity in the city, where fearful Zairean troops have stolen aid agency vehicles and robbed foreigners.
"There were 128 passengers aboard the two Buffalo aircraft from Bukavu -- U.N., NGOs (Non-Governmental Organisations) and we believe some other foreign nationals," said Barton.
The last foreign aid workers were evacuated from the eastern Zairean town of Uvira, south of Bukavu, last Tuesday. Burundian military sources said on Saturday it had fallen to ethnic Tutsi rebels.
